The present information indicates the addition of hydroelectric facilities at Amistad Dam will cause no reduction in the average total energy generated by the Eagle Pass plant, and may result in some increase in total generation.
4.49 The proposed integrated system operation of Amistad and Falcon Reservoirs will result on the average in the Falcon Reservoir level being slightly higher and the Amistad Reservoir being slightly lower. The total annual reservoir evaporation loss under the proposed operation is slightly more than with the operation of the two reservoirs without hydropower at Amistad. 4.50 The indicated annual difference of 2,000 acre-feet a year by the proposed operation is only 0.1 percent of the annual regulated supply. This theoretical small change is not considered significant as the hydrology studies do not have the capability to predict accurately at this level. Essentially, these results show that the addition of Amistad Reservoir increased the average annual regulated supply by about 205,000 acre-feet per year, and the addition of the hydro plant at Amistad does not materially change the regulated supply.
Installation of Hydropower by Mexico
4.51 Although the proposed action entails adding hydropower facilities only on the United States side of Amistad Dam, there is the probability that Mexico may add similar facilities in the future. The present proposal can be referred to as an interim condition (i.e., two units on the US side) and the future condition can be referred to as an ultimate condition (i.e., two units on the US side and two units on the Mexican side). Maximum discharges for the interim condition are estimated to range from 3,800 to 4,500 cfs, averaging about 4,000 cfs, and maximum discharges for the ultimate condition are estimated to be about 9,000 cfs. The same volume of water would be passed through turbines, but the time required to pass it would be less than half as long. It should be noted that a flow of 9,000 cfs represents a condition whereby both powerhouses would be operated at full capacity simultaneously; but this condition of electrical demand may not necessarily occur routinely on a day to day basis. A 9,000 cfs release represents the maximum condition that may occur occasionally.
4.52 In anticipation of both the interim and the ultimate conditions (i.e., two US units versus two US and two Mexican units), test releases were made in April 1976 to check the difference in these two flow conditions in the Rio Grande channel below the dam.
